tool.name: fingerprint_tech_stack
tool.description:
Detect the target's tech stack and auto-load the matching strix skills into this agent's prompt context.
This tool is the deterministic complement to the agent's `load_skill` decision-making. When the target's stack is unambiguous (X-Powered-By: Next.js, Firebase JS SDK in body, Set-Cookie: laravel_session=..., etc.), the relevant skill loads automatically — no follow-up load_skill call needed.
Mechanism: 1-2 cheap HTTP requests (HEAD + GET, 8s timeout each) to the target's root URL. Parses response headers, Set-Cookie, and a 32 KiB body window for well-known tech-stack markers. For each high-confidence detection that maps to a strix skill, calls the same skill-loader as `load_skill`. Caps loaded skills at 5 (the same limit load_skill enforces).
When to use: ALWAYS at the start of recon for any web target. The output gives you the tech stack to reason about plus the skills you can rely on being loaded going forward. For pure DNS/domain recon (no HTTP probing), this tool is not the right fit — use dns_hygiene_check + subdomain_takeover_check instead.
Categories of detection: web frameworks (Next.js, NestJS, FastAPI, Express, Django, Rails, Laravel, ASP.NET, PHP), CMS (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, Shopify), JS frameworks (React, Angular, Vue, Nuxt), Backend-as-a-Service (Firebase, Supabase), CDN/WAF (Cloudflare, Akamai), and via deep mode: GraphQL endpoints.
Side effect: skills get loaded into the agent's prompt. `skills_loaded` in the return value is the authoritative list of what landed.

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: Full URL to probe, e.g. "https://example.com/" or "http://api.example.com:8080/". Domain-only inputs are auto-prefixed with https://. The tool always probes the root URL (`/`), regardless of any path component supplied.

parameter.name: deep
parameter.description: When true, also POST a focused GraphQL introspection probe to common paths (/graphql, /api/graphql, /v1/graphql, /graphiql). Default false to keep network footprint minimal.

returns.description:
{success, target, probe_url, http_status, technologies: [...], recommended_skills, skills_loaded, newly_loaded_skills, skill_load_error}.
Each entry in `technologies` is {technology, label, confidence (high|medium|low), evidence, [version], [skill]}.
`skills_loaded` is the authoritative list of skills now in the agent's prompt context.
